correctness.rationale: Character modulation puts a peak at zero; normalize source mass to 1 and use H=q f̂, so H(0)=1 without changing the quotient. Existence follows by coercivity, and strict real convexity of Σ|H|⁴ plus Fourier invertibility yields uniqueness. Symmetry forces the optimizer to the center and punctured-axis orbits. For x=qb the Fourier values on the three classes are 1, 1−x, 1−2x. Removing Im x strictly lowers energy unless it is zero; the real derivative equation is (x−1)³+(q−1)(2x−1)³=0, whose solution is (1+s)/(1+2s), s³=q−1. The two nonzero-frequency magnitudes are <1 and the fourth-power sum is 1+(q−1)²/(1+2s)³. This proves attainment and, by uniqueness after normalization, the full complex equality family. The center and arm values coincide only if s=q−1, i.e. q=2; the central numerator decreases for q≥2 and changes sign between 5 and 6. At q=9 the seed is (−1/15,1/15); the spectrum gives 1+16(2/5)⁴+64(1/5)⁴=189/125. The leading growth of the fourth-power sum is q/8. The phrase ‘three distinct values’ in the proof should mean values on three frequency classes for a general x (at x=0 all coincide), with no effect on the valid quartic or on the distinct optimal values. The supplied checker.py, including its F₉ trace and multiplicities, was read, not run.
